title: Interview Flow Fabric — Calibration Journal & Micro-rubric
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic journal for designing, calibrating, and iterating interview flows across hiring panels. Goal is to reduce variance between interviewers, speed async debriefs, and ensure handoffs to onboarding include concrete, prioritized evidence. Treat as a living notebook — short notes, TODOs, and explicit calibration actions.

Scope:
- Roles: software engineers (IC1–IC4), infra/SRE, applied ML; adaptable to other tracks.
- Stages covered: phone screen -> technical panel -> hiring manager sync -> offer recommendation -> week-zero onboarding handoff.
- Audience: interviewers, hiring managers, people-ops partners, recruiting coordinators.

Quick summary (one-liner for coordinators):
Use the micro-rubric below during each panel slot, capture 3 evidence bullets (behavioral, technical, signal-of-growth), then submit async score + top-2 concerns in the candidate thread within 24 hours. If >2 concerns or conflicting signals, schedule a 30-minute calibration sync.

Pre-panel checklist (for panel lead / host):
- Confirm problem statement and time splits (e.g., 10m litmus q, 35m system-design, 15m culture/role fit).
- Share prompt and expected answer notes to panel Slack thread 24h ahead.
- Assign Scribe and Evidence Lead (scribe captures exact candidate wording; Evidence Lead reframes into evidence bullets).
- Verify interview environment (Zoom link, whiteboard access, recording policy).
- If remote candidate timezone differences, ensure explicit timeboxing and water breaks.

The Micro-rubric (use per-interviewer, 1–4 scale):
- Problem framing (1-4): did candidate clarify constraints, ask clarifying Qs, propose evaluation metrics?
- Solution decomposition (1-4): ability to split bigger problems into orthogonal subproblems; tradeoffs considered.
- Correctness & implementation plan (1-4): correct core approach + feasible implementation steps for first 30 days.
- Operational sense (1-4): observability, failure modes, deploy/rollback considerations (SRE/infra emphasis).
- Communication & teamwork (1-4): clarity, listen/respond to hints, accepts and integrates feedback.
- Learning velocity signal (1-4): evidence candidate can iterate quickly and improve from feedback.

Evidence capture template (3 short bullets, required):
- Behavioral evidence: exact quote and scenario (e.g., “led postmortem on payment outage, prioritized backlog to fix the race condition”).
- Technical evidence: concrete artifact of skill (e.g., described consistent hashing tradeoffs and wrote a pseudo-shard rebalance).
- Growth/unknowns evidence: primary gap to watch and learning plan (e.g., unfamiliar with X, likely to ramp in 4 weeks with mentor pairing).

Async debrief protocol (must follow):
1) Within 24h submit: numeric average (1–4) per micro-rubric area, 3 evidence bullets, top-2 hiring risks, recommendation {strong-yes | yes | borderline | no}.
2) If any interviewer marks a 1 in Communication or Correctness, they must add an explicit example.
3) If recommendations vary by more than one step (e.g., yes vs no) or two or more "top risks" overlap, tag the hiring manager + people-ops and request a 30m sync.

Calibration entries (how we log changes over time):
- 2025-05-27: tightened "Operational sense" descriptor for infra candidates — added explicit observability probes example.
- 2025-08-12: trialed 1–5 scale with applied-ml panels; reverted to 1–4 to reduce anchoring drift.
- 2025-10-03: added mandatory Evidence Lead role; reduced scribe burden.
(Keep short bulleted history at top of doc for auditability.)

Decision heuristics (concrete shortcuts for hiring managers):
- Fast-approve: average rubric >=3.5, no category <3, no >1 risk, strong-yes from hiring manager -> offer.
- Needs-manager-review: average 3.0–3.49 or one category at 2 with clear mitigation plan -> schedule manager sync.
- Decline: average <2.5 or two categories at 1 or repeated factual inconsistencies.

Hand-off to onboarding (what recruiting/people-ops must deliver):
- Consolidated 3-bullet evidence pack (from Evidence Lead) + concrete week-0 tasks (3 tasks mapped to candidate strengths).
- Access matrix: repo access, infra sandbox, Slack channels, calendar invites for onboarding cohort.
- Mentor pairing recommendation and initial 30/60/90 goals (short bullet list).
- Known blockers and expected ramp timeline.

Operational notes / smells to watch (notes-to-self style):
- Interviewers often drift to whiteboard polish; enforce first 20 minutes for framing + tradeoffs.
- Evidence bullets tend to be vague; always require a direct quote or artifact reference.
- Async debriefs late (>48h) correlate with candidate ghosting and offer declines.

Quick templates (copy-paste into the candidate thread):
- Async debrief header: \"Panel debrief — <Candidate Name> — Role\"
- Rubric line: \"PF:3 / SD:4 / CI:3 / OP:2 / COM:3 / LV:3 -> avg 3.0 | rec: needs-manager-review\"
- Evidence bullets: 1) \"Behavioral: \"...\"\" 2) \"Technical: ...\" 3) \"Growth: ...\"

Open TODOs (for next 8 weeks):
- Build a short Loom for new interviewers on Evidence Lead role (owner: Sara, due 2025-11-15).
- Extract anonymized evidence examples into a training deck (owner: Liam, backlog PR created).
- Add a one-click Confluence macro to render the micro-rubric in the candidate page (owner: Diego).

Appendix: example debrief (realistic but anonymized)
- Candidate: \"A\" — Staff SRE candidate. Panel debrief summary: PF:4 / SD:3 / CI:3 / OP:4 / COM:4 / LV:4 -> avg 3.67 | rec: strong-yes. Evidence bullets: (1) led migration off legacy queue under SLA 3x improvement, quote: \"I prioritized idempotency and routed fallback to dead-letter queue\"; (2) implemented canary + rollout plan; (3) main gap: k8s ops experience, plan: 2-week pairing with infra.

Notes to new users of this doc: keep entries short, timestamp calibration changes, and prefer concrete artifacts over adjectives (avoid: "strong engineer").
